items.title: Market Selloff and Tech Sector Weakness
points: Nasdaq Composite fell 10% last week and S&P 500 dropped 8.6%, the worst weekly performance in years, as AI (artificial intelligence, technology that learns from data to make predictions and decisions) investment enthusiasm reversed.
AI and semiconductor infrastructure stocks bore the brunt of selling, suggesting investors are reassessing valuations in the high-flying tech space.
Dell earnings Tuesday will be closely watched for AI server order backlogs and profit margins (revenue minus costs), indicating whether the AI infrastructure spending cycle remains healthy.

items.title: Inflation Data and Federal Reserve Implications
points: Core PCE (Personal Consumption Expenditures, an inflation measure excluding volatile food and energy prices) is expected to rise 3.2% year-over-year in November, the final inflation reading before the Fed's December 8-9 policy meeting.
Wednesday also brings durable goods orders, a revised Q3 GDP estimate, and the Fed's Beige Book (a qualitative summary of economic conditions from Federal Reserve districts).
The reading is seen as critical for markets seeking clarity on whether the Fed pauses rate cuts or adjusts its policy trajectory.

items.title: Holiday Consumer Demand and Retail Signals
points: A CivicScience survey shows 40% of shoppers plan to visit stores in person on Black Friday, the highest level since 2014.
Gen Z consumers are expected to lead the rebound in in-store shopping traffic, signaling potential strength for retailers like Best Buy, Dollar Tree, and HP.
U.S. markets close Thursday for Thanksgiving and at 1 p.m. Friday, limiting trading activity that week.

items.title: Closed-End Fund Valuations and Income Opportunities
points: Closed-end fund (CEF, a mutual fund with a fixed number of shares that trade on exchanges like stocks) discounts have widened to a median 9.67% discount to net asset value (NAV, a fund's per-share holdings value), the widest since April 2024.
Nearly 46% of all CEFs now trade at discounts exceeding 10%, with fixed-income and real estate funds hit hardest, largely due to valuation compression rather than portfolio deterioration.
Historically, steep discount periods have been followed by substantial recoveries, potentially rewarding patient income investors who can tolerate short-term volatility.
Analysis highlights specific deeply discounted funds while urging careful selection and diversification across interest-rate environments.

items.title: Anthropic's Historic IPO and Market Reception
points: Anthropic's IPO raised $81 billion at a $1.2 trillion valuation, surpassing SpaceX's $75 billion 2024 raise to become the largest IPO in history.
Shares opened at $111.50 on Thursday, $28.50 above the $83 IPO price, then fell to close Friday at $88, below the offer price.
Trading began on Nasdaq at 11:45 a.m. ET under ticker ANT, earlier than many market watchers expected.

items.title: Media Access Restrictions and Controversy
points: Anthropic barred journalists from the Nasdaq trading booth during its IPO, contrary to standard market practice of media broadcasting from the exchange.
The company cited its own preferences, but the move contradicted its public transparency positioning and drew internal employee dissent.
Observers and media outlets expressed surprise, viewing the decision as misaligned with Anthropic's stated values of openness.

items.title: Nvidia's Internal Crisis During Leadership Transition
points: Interim CEO Colette Kress held Nvidia's first company-wide meeting without founder Jensen Huang, offering raises and added stock compensation to address workforce concerns.
Kress did not take direct employee questions during the all-hands meeting, a departure from typical practice that drew further employee criticism on social media.
The company is trying to stabilize morale amid uncertainty over leadership direction following Huang's departure.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: Wall Street just had a bizarre, wild week

headlines: Anthropic's IPO raised $81 billion at a $1.2 trillion valuation, dethroning SpaceX as the largest IPO in history, though the stock fell from opening day highs to close Friday below the offer price.
The AI lab restricted media access to the Nasdaq trading floor on IPO day, a move that surprised observers given the company's stated focus on transparency and drew criticism from employees.

Nvidia faces a leadership crisis even as founder Jensen Huang steps aside; interim CEO Colette Kress held an all-hands meeting focused on damage control with promises of raises and stock bonuses, but did not take direct employee questions.
The contrasting fortunes of Anthropic and Nvidia this week highlight the volatility and tension within the AI industry despite continued market enthusiasm.
